title: Flat bow or twisted bow?
hook: Two bows in the same laces: one lies flat, one twists. Which comes undone first?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that tying the second stage the opposite way to the first gives a bow that lies flat across the shoe (a reef bow), while tying both the same way gives a granny bow that twists toe-to-heel and comes loose more easily

misconception: A bow is a bow: the direction of the first knot doesn't change how well it holds.
objective: Opposing knot stages make the balanced reef bow lie flat; the granny bow twists out of line. Impact and moving lace ends can work a bow loose.

claims.text: The twisted bow comes from tying both knot stages the same way round; tying the second the opposite way makes the bow lie flat. To read your own: a flat bow lies flat, a twisted bow twists out of line.

claims.text: A bow that twists out of line is the sign of matching stages. Making the second stage right-over-left opposes the first and gives the balanced bow that tends to lie flat. It can still fail; the drawing is not a tying tutorial. (Recall question: 'Both stages of your knot are left-over-right, and the finished bow twists out of line.' Keyed option: 'Make the second stage right-over-left'.)
claims.source: Daily-Diamond, Gregg and O'Reilly (2017), 'The roles of impact and inertia in the failure of a shoelace knot', Proc R Soc A 473: 20160770 (PMC5415684): strong knot based on the square knot (two trefoils of opposite handedness); weak knot is the granny, where 'the two trefoils have the same handedness, causing the knot to twist instead of laying flat'; impact of the shoe loosens the knot and whipping of the free ends produces slipping. No shoe-relative direction is claimed (that rested on Fieggen, fieggen.com, not reachable). The keyed option is the only one that opposes the first stage. | Before the 2026-10-15 rewording: Ian Fieggen, Granny Knot Info, https://www.fieggen.com/shoelace/grannyknot.htm (opened 2026-10-14), balanced/opposing stages and bow orientation; Daily-Diamond, Gregg & O'Reilly 2017, doi:10.1098/rspa.2016.0770, full paper opened at https://escholarship.org/content/qt7qs984k7/qt7qs984k7_noSplash_66a8485e2a04a2d12bd2baeb463325cf.pdf. The model step decrements are illustrative, not data. Scenario values in the recall question are stipulated. Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, 2026-10-14), applied by session 1. FC LH-3B (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): left unverified because the source could not be opened. The egress policy blocks www.fieggen.com and the escholarship.org PDF (proxy 403). Wikipedia (Shoelace knot) and Fieggen quotes in search snippets agree: matching stages give a granny bow that sits vertically/along the shoe, opposing stages give a reef bow that sits across it. The keyed option is the only one that opposes the stages; the why keeps "can still fail". Re-check from a connected host. See company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH3-2026-10-14.md (Batch B). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD UNVERIFIED. Same source dependency as c1: the recall why's claim that matching stages give a bow along the shoe and opposing stages one across it is a fact about real knots, from unopened sources (DNS, proxy 403). The keyed option (second stage right-over-left) is the only one that opposes a left-over-right first stage, so the logic is consistent. The physical claim is unchecked. Left unverified. | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD. Same sources as c1 (unreachable). The keyed option is the only one that opposes a left-over-right first stage. Opened Daily-Diamond, Gregg & O'Reilly 2017, Proc R Soc A 473:20160770, full text via the PMC OAI API (GetRecord oai:pubmedcentral.nih.gov:5415684, fetched 2026-10-16, sha256 34a718bc084c…): 'The strong version of this knot is based on the square knot: two trefoil knots of opposite handedness are stacked …'; 'the granny … the two trefoils have the same handedness, causing the knot to twist instead of laying flat when tightened'. A right-over-left stage is the mirror of left-over-right, so it has the opposite handedness: the keyed option ('Make the second stage right-over-left') is the only one that gives opposite-handed stages, and 'can still fail' agrees with the paper.
claims.note: FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): UNVERIFIED. HELD. Same orientation dependency as c1. 'A bow lying along the shoe is the sign of matching stages' needs Fieggen (403). Daily-Diamond et al. 2017 (PMC5415684, opened) confirms matching handedness = granny = twisted, and opposite handedness = square-based = flat, but gives no shoe-relative direction. The keyed option (reverse the second stage) is the only one that opposes the first stage. Fix: as c1, describe the sign as 'twisted' rather than 'along the shoe', or open Fieggen. | Reset to unverified by demo-builder (2026-10-15): W-938 / FC41 rewording applied: the sign is now 'twists out of line' / 'lie flat' (recall question and why) instead of 'along the shoe' / 'across the shoe'. | FC pass 42 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Recall: both stages left-over-right, the bow twists out of line; key 'Make the second stage right-over-left'. PMC5415684 (opened): 'The difference between the knots lies in the handedness ... of the "second trefoil": that is, "left over right" or "right over left." In the strong knot, the handedness of the second trefoil is different from the first'. Same handedness gives the granny, which twists 'instead of laying flat'. 'It can still fail' agrees with the paper, which compares weak and strong knot failure rates (both fail). Distractors (tighter, a third matching stage) do not change the second stage's handedness.
